description: CyberGiants is a team of young innovators passionate about technology, coding, science, and problem-solving. For NASA Space Apps 2026, we aim to develop health monitoring software that helps astronauts track health indicators during space missions. We welcome members skilled or interested in software development, UI/UX design, AI, data analysis, health sciences, and research.
summary:
**AstroTwin Sentinel** is an offline-first astronaut wellness monitoring system designed to support crew health awareness during long-duration space missions, including journeys to Mars.

The project combines three core technologies: a webcam-based blink sensor powered by Google MediaPipe, a local AI Medical Officer called Dr. Sentinel powered by Ollama, and a Crew Audio Log that records voice journals and analyzes acoustic indicators such as RMS, peak amplitude, and loudness. It also provides mission records, historical trends, user profiles, and secure personal data management.

AstroTwin Sentinel addresses the challenge of monitoring astronaut wellness in isolated environments where communication with Earth may be delayed or unavailable. By combining local sensing, AI-assisted guidance, and accessible health records, it helps astronauts observe selected wellness patterns and review changes over time without depending on continuous internet access.

Our vision is to make astronaut wellness monitoring more accessible, privacy-conscious, and suitable for increasingly autonomous space missions.
details:
AstroTwin Sentinel Project Details

1. What the Project Does

AstroTwin Sentinel is an offline-first astronaut wellness monitoring system designed to support crew health awareness during long-duration space missions, particularly missions to Mars. It addresses two major challenges of space exploration: the difficulty of continuously monitoring astronaut wellness and the dependence on Earth-based assistance when communication is delayed or unavailable.

Our solution transforms existing computer equipment, such as a tablet or laptop camera and microphone, into a lightweight wellness-monitoring interface. Instead of depending entirely on additional wearable devices, the system uses computer vision, acoustic analysis, and locally running artificial intelligence to help astronauts observe selected wellness indicators and review changes over time.

2. How the System Works

AstroTwin Sentinel consists of three interconnected components:

A. Live Webcam Blink Sensor

The system uses Google MediaPipe Face Landmarker to track facial landmarks through a webcam. It applies the Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) algorithm to estimate eye closure and detect blink events. A rolling 60-second calculation produces an experimental blink-rate estimate in blinks per minute.

The sensor uses hysteresis, a minimum eye-closure duration, and a cooldown period to reduce false blink counts. Measurements are displayed in real time and recorded for historical review.

B. Dr. Sentinel — Local AI Medical Officer

Dr. Sentinel is powered by the lightweight Llama 3.2:1b model through Ollama. It processes the measured blink-rate value and generates a short response using predefined prototype rules.

Unlike cloud-dependent AI services, the local model can operate without an internet connection when the application and Ollama are running on the same machine. This supports faster local responses and reduces dependence on communication with Earth.

C. Crew Audio Log

The Crew Audio Log provides an environment for astronauts to record personal voice journals. Using the Web Audio API, it displays a live waveform and calculates acoustic measurements, including Root Mean Square (RMS), peak amplitude, and dBFS loudness.

Users can record, review, play back, discard, and add written notes to their recordings. Audio remains local until the user explicitly chooses to save it to their account.

3. Dashboard and Mission Records

The platform organizes its functionality into three main sections:

  • Live Assessment: Provides the webcam feed, real-time blink telemetry, sensor status, session timer, and Dr. Sentinel diagnostic action.
  • Crew Audio Log: Provides voice recording, live waveform visualization, acoustic measurements, and a notes editor.
  • Mission Records & Trends: Displays historical blink-rate charts, previous AI responses, acoustic records, and saved audio logs. Users can review or delete previous records.

The system also supports astronaut profiles, authentication, secure personal records, and user-specific data access through Row-Level Security (RLS).

4. Benefits and Intended Impact

AstroTwin Sentinel aims to make selected astronaut wellness indicators easier to observe, record, and review during isolated missions.

Its main benefits include:

  • Reduced monitoring friction: Uses existing cameras and microphones instead of requiring additional wearable equipment for the implemented features.
  • Local AI assistance: Allows the diagnostic component to operate without continuous internet connectivity.
  • Privacy-conscious monitoring: Gives users control over when audio recordings are saved.
  • Continuous record keeping: Maintains historical sessions and trends for personal review.
  • Greater crew autonomy: Supports astronauts in observing their wellness patterns when immediate communication with Earth is limited.
  • Expandable architecture: Provides a foundation for integrating additional validated health indicators in future development.

Beyond space exploration, the offline-first approach could eventually be adapted for remote research stations, isolated medical facilities, ships, and other environments where connectivity is unreliable.

5. Technologies and Tools Used

The project was developed using modern web technologies and open-source tools:

Frontend and Application Development

  • TanStack Start v1
  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS v4

Computer Vision

  • Google MediaPipe Face Landmarker
  • WebAssembly
  • Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR) algorithm

Artificial Intelligence

  • Ollama
  • Llama 3.2:1b
  • Local AI inference

Audio Processing

  • Web Audio API
  • MediaRecorder API
  • Real-time waveform visualization
  • RMS, peak amplitude, and dBFS calculations

Backend and Data Management

  • Lovable Cloud
  • Managed database
  • User authentication
  • Google sign-in
  • Private file storage
  • Row-Level Security (RLS)

Development and Collaboration

  • Lovable
  • GitHub
  • Bun package manager
  • Automated testing

6. What Makes the Project Creative?

The creativity of AstroTwin Sentinel lies in combining computer vision, local artificial intelligence, acoustic monitoring, and personal mission records within one integrated wellness platform.

Rather than treating these technologies as separate applications, we designed a unified console that connects live sensor readings, local AI-generated guidance, voice journaling, and historical trends.

Another important innovation is the offline-first architecture. Conventional AI applications frequently depend on remote cloud services. AstroTwin Sentinel demonstrates how a lightweight AI model can run locally, making the diagnostic feature available without requiring continuous communication with Earth.

The project also emphasizes user privacy and control through local processing and authenticated, user-specific records.

7. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several factors when designing the solution:

  • Spaceflight conditions: Isolation, confinement, distance from Earth, and the challenges of long-duration missions.
  • Connectivity limitations: The system should not depend on continuous internet access for local sensing and local AI inference.
  • Resource efficiency: We selected lightweight tools and models suitable for ordinary computing hardware.
  • Privacy and security: Personal wellness records require authentication, controlled access, and secure storage.
  • Usability: Information should be presented through clear indicators, charts, and accessible dashboard sections.
  • Scientific limitations: Camera-derived blink rates and acoustic measurements must be treated cautiously because they are not independently validated medical diagnoses.
  • Future adaptability: The system should allow additional validated indicators and improved AI capabilities to be integrated over time.

8. Testing, Limitations, and Future Development

The current prototype has a reported record of 18 out of 18 automated tests passing, covering key software functionality such as eye-aspect-ratio calculations, audio metrics, and review generation.

However, passing software tests does not establish clinical accuracy. Blink-rate thresholds are experimental prototype rules, and acoustic measurements are not validated indicators of psychological conditions.

Future development will focus on integrating additional health measurements, establishing individual wellness baselines, improving sensor reliability across different environmental conditions, and validating the system through controlled testing and expert review.

NASA's Human Research Program resources and research into behavioral health monitoring informed our understanding of the challenges astronauts face. The current prototype does not directly ingest a NASA health dataset.

Our Vision

AstroTwin Sentinel represents our vision of a more autonomous approach to astronaut wellness: a system that helps crews observe selected health-related patterns, preserve their records, and access local AI assistance even when Earth is far away.

AstroTwin Sentinel — Your Digital Guardian Beyond Earth.
